summary: India runs one of the world's largest eVisa programs: citizens of around 170 countries can apply online for tourist eVisas valid 30 days, 1 year or 5 years, starting at 25 USD. Applications go exclusively through the official indianvisaonline.gov.in portal.

passportValidity.text: Your passport must be valid for at least 6 months from the date of arrival and have at least 2 blank pages. The e-Visa instructions put the six months at the time of applying, while the same page's FAQ and the UK Foreign Office count them from arrival — the stricter reading, used here.

vaccinations.name: Yellow fever
vaccinations.text: Travellers arriving by air or sea within 6 days of being in, or transiting through, a yellow fever endemic country (India notifies 30 in Africa and 13 in South America) must carry a valid yellow fever certificate (ICVP). Without one you can be quarantined for up to 6 days — India enforces this strictly. Infants under six months are exempt.

source.name: Bureau of Immigration, India — Health Regulation

vaccinations.name: Polio (OPV/IPV)
vaccinations.text: Resident nationals travelling from polio-endemic countries (Afghanistan, Nigeria, Pakistan) and from countries with imported poliovirus circulation (Democratic Republic of the Congo, Ethiopia, Kenya, Somalia, Syria) must show proof of oral polio vaccination taken at least 4 weeks before departure.

source.name: WHO — Vaccination requirements and recommendations for international travellers, country list (ITH 2022)

travelInsurance.text: No official source we could read states a travel-insurance requirement for India. The UK Foreign Office advises checking before you travel that you have appropriate travel insurance for local treatment or unexpected medical evacuation.

source.name: UK FCDO — India travel advice: health

onwardTicket.text: eVisa applicants must hold a return or onward ticket and sufficient funds for the stay.

source.name: Indian Visa Online — e-Visa eligibility, instructions and FAQ (Bureau of Immigration)

proofOfFunds.text: You must have sufficient money to support yourself during the stay; no fixed amount is published, but immigration may ask.

notes: Duty-free allowance: 100 cigarettes and 2 litres of alcohol, plus new goods worth up to ₹25,000 for tourists of foreign origin (₹75,000 for residents and tourists of Indian origin) under the Baggage Rules, 2026.

The UK Foreign Office says it is illegal to possess or operate satellite phones and GPS devices in India without a licence, even in transit; devices can be confiscated and you can be fined or arrested.

payments.text: The UK government's travel advice says you can bring cash, travellers cheques or a bank card and exchange or withdraw rupees in India. No official source we could read describes how widely cards are accepted for payment.

safety.text: Most visits are trouble-free, but petty crime, traffic and scams around tourist sites warrant increased caution. Women travelers should take particular care, especially at night. The UK advises against all travel within 10 km of the Pakistan border and to Jammu and Kashmir (except travel by air to and within the city of Jammu), and against all but essential travel to Manipur.

bestTimeToVisit.text: Canada's travel advice says the monsoon season runs from June to September, when heavy rain can cause flooding and landslides across the country; the UK's says it usually runs from June to October. Canada adds that India's coastline is subject to cyclones, particularly between April and December.

idp.text: India is a party to the 1949 Geneva Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1968 Vienna one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1949 Geneva version. A permit issued under the 1968 Vienna Convention carries no treaty obligation here.

tips.text: Apply only at indianvisaonline.gov.in — look-alike sites charge large markups and some are outright scams.
Carry a printed copy of your eVisa approval (ETA) — airlines and immigration ask for it.
Canada's travel advice says special permits are required to visit parts of India designated as restricted or protected areas; India's Bureau of Immigration lists them.
Canada's travel advice says travellers' diarrhoea is the most common illness affecting travellers. Its rule of thumb: boil it, cook it, peel it, or leave it.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for India?
faq.answer: Yes. US passport holders need a visa for India; most tourists use the e-Tourist Visa (30 days, 1 year or 5 years), applied for online at indianvisaonline.gov.in. Apply at least 4 days before travel.

faq.question: How much does an India eVisa cost?
faq.answer: The 30-day e-Tourist Visa has a standard fee of 25 USD (10 USD for April–June arrivals), the 1-year version 40 USD, and the 5-year version 200 USD. Fees differ for a few nationalities. The official portal shows your exact fee before payment.

faq.question: How long does the India eVisa take?
faq.answer: Most eVisas are approved within 1–4 business days. Apply at least 4 days before your flight; you cannot use the eVisa scheme more than twice per calendar year for the 30-day version.

faq.question: Do I need vaccinations to enter India?
faq.answer: Only conditionally: a yellow fever certificate if you arrive from a risk country (strictly enforced — quarantine applies without it), and a polio vaccination certificate if arriving from a polio-affected country. No vaccinations are required when flying directly from Europe, the Americas or most of Asia.

faq.question: Can I extend an India eVisa?
faq.answer: Tourist eVisas cannot be extended. For longer stays, use the 1-year or 5-year multiple-entry eVisa (max 90 days per visit for most nationalities) or a regular embassy visa.
